score.note: First structural draft, not a permutation search. Full read of games/gs1/asm/080dd2c4.s plus out/family-transplants/main-080dd2c4/m2c/target.canonical.s / 080dd2c4.c (m2c's raw decompile of the actual retained bytes), cross-checked instruction-by-instruction against the family template (member_orbit/run.c, owner 080ce85c) and against 080e7404.c's documented idioms. Textually the candidate is very close: --asm reports candidate_insns=497 vs reference_insns=503 (only 6 net), and the generated .s (read in full from --work output) is structurally sound throughout -- correct field offsets, correct trampoline-indirect-call modeling, correct table types -- with no unresolved M2C_ERROR/M2C_FIELD placeholders. The large differing_halfwords count is dominated by a single register-allocation choice diverging at the very first opportunity (the reference keeps the persistent work-block pointer in fp for the whole function; this candidate's allocator puts the innermost loop counter -- reused across the spC-inner loop and the final 0x200-entry particle loop -- in fp instead, and work in r9, an exact role-swap of the two), which cascades into every subsequent pc-relative literal-pool offset and several stack-slot assignments for the rest of the function. This is the same fp/r9 (and sl/r9) 'known open, not-source-shape-controllable' residual already documented at length in this family's sibling dossiers (see games/gs1/recon/en/main/080dc1ec.json score.note, prior_note_2026_08_27c/d: ~8 targeted reshapes tried there to flip an analogous swap, all either no-op or regressed). Given that precedent this pass did not run an open-ended register-forcing search; two cheap, legitimate fixes were applied and kept (see rejected_experiments/notes) but the fp/r9 swap itself was not chased further.
score.fixes_applied: (1) The two Data_03001e50[46]/[47] reads that seed rectangle[0]/rectangle[1] must go through the plain Data_03001e50 global directly, not through the heap_cache local established at function entry -- heap_cache's register is dead again by the time these reads happen (several intervening calls), so the reference re-loads the 0x03001e50 base fresh via its own literal-pool entry; routing through heap_cache[7]/heap_cache[8] instead produced an extra redundant address computation. (2) mode (arg1, spilled to sp+44 in the retained assembly's very first instruction) must be declared textually BEFORE draw_destination among the locals, not after, to land mode/draw_destination on the reference's sp+44/sp+40 slots respectively -- this alone raised matched_prefix from 8 to 14 and dropped differing_halfwords from 589 to 505.

Semantic summary: a battle-presentation sub-effect on the same 0x03001eec work-block subsystem as member_orbit, taking (object, mode). Seeds a 1024-slot particle pool at 0x02010018 (stride 28, field 0x18=-1 marks a slot free) and a 16-entry per-index table at work+0x7080 (positions/heights seeded from Func_08004458() and clamped against Data_080eeb4b[Func_080022fc(i,3)]), then runs a byte-table-bounded (Data_080eeb5e[object->0x18]) sequence of frames. Each frame conditionally shows a HUD countdown near the end, and -- while more than 4 frames remain -- runs a nested spC-inner loop (bounded by the same Data_080eeb5e byte) that: sometimes toggles work->0x77A8, draws a rectangle through rectangle_slot[1 & idx] using one of two parallel Data_080eeb4[48/4E]/[54/58] table pairs selected by mode (with an extra Data_080eeb71 clamp in the mode!=0 case), dispatches Func_080d6888 once per listed member (object field 0x24, stride 2, object field 0x14 count) at a specific milestone frame, and at two other milestones claims one free slot from a SEPARATE 512-slot pool at 0x02010000. Every frame, unconditionally, also walks that whole 512-slot pool drawing any active slot's particle twice (via rectangle[0] then rectangle[1] directly, not by parity) with a decaying lifetime field, before flagging work->0x7824 and yielding a frame via Func_080030f8(1).
No GS2 or external source was used; no other Golden Sun decompilation project was consulted.
